answer_1.quote: We provide a popular real-world example of image transcreation in Figure , where content was recreated to match cultural norms of a target audience.
answer_1.outputs: transcreated images adapted from a source culture to a target culture

answer_2.quote: we propose three metrics that account for the varied dimensions of this subjective task -a) Object-based; b) Embedding-based and c) VLM-based metrics, each of which leverages powerful open and closed VLMs and Large Language Models (LLMs).

answer_3.quote: Finally, similar to LLM-based scores for text, we can prompt VLMs to assign a score on a fixed scale to estimate how far the model has transcreated the source image for cultural relevance; how semantically equivalent is the transcreated image to the source image; and how they fare on visual similarity.
methods: prompting VLMs to assign scores on a fixed scale

answer_4.quote: all outputs are given a rating on a scale of 1-5 by human annotators, across multiple dimensions including visual change, semantic equivalence, cultural relevance, naturalness and offensiveness.
answer_4.guideline: Questions from the evaluation set of used for meta-evaluation in this work. Does the image seem like it came from your country / is representative of your culture? Is the generated image from the same semantic category as the original image? Is there any visual change in the generated image compared to the original image?
